examples.name: A scope selector
examples.description: The common case - independent on/off search chips sharing one size. Chip Group lays them out; the consumer holds which are on.

examples.name: An active filter bar
examples.description: Filter chips share the group's size; removing one is the consumer's job.
examples.jsx:
<ChipGroup size="md" aria-label="Active filters">
  <Chip
    mode="filter"
    label="Status"
    elemBefore={<TaskNotStartedIcon decorative />}
    value={{ label: '2 statuses', sections: statusSections }}
    onRemove={() => dropFilter('status')}
  />
  <Chip
    mode="filter"
    label="Due date"
    elemBefore={<CalendarIcon decorative />}
    operator={{ label: 'before', sections: operatorSections }}
    value={{ label: 'April 15', sections: dateSections }}
    onRemove={() => dropFilter('due')}
  />
</ChipGroup>

examples.name: Packing chips against the trailing edge
examples.description: alignment maps to justify-content - which edge the chips pack against. Note this is not Tag Group's alignment, which places an overflow tag.
examples.jsx:
<ChipGroup alignment="right" size="md">
  <Chip mode="search" label="Matters" isSelected />
  <Chip mode="search" label="Documents" />
</ChipGroup>

examples.name: One chip opting out of the group's size
examples.description: An explicit size on an individual Chip wins, because Chip resolves size ?? groupSize ?? 'md'.
examples.jsx:
<ChipGroup size="sm">
  <Chip mode="search" label="Inherits sm" />
  <Chip mode="search" label="Explicitly md" size="md" />
</ChipGroup>

examples.name: Size reaching a wrapped chip
examples.description: Size travels by context, so it still reaches a Chip behind a Tooltip, a fragment, or a conditional - which cloning children would not.
examples.jsx:
<ChipGroup size="sm">
  <Tooltip content="Only matters you own">
    <Chip mode="search" label="My matters" />
  </Tooltip>
  {showArchived ? <Chip mode="search" label="Archived" /> : null}
</ChipGroup>

examples.name: Mixed modes in one group
examples.description: Any Chip mode can share a row - the group only lays them out and shares a size.
examples.jsx:
<ChipGroup size="md">
  <Chip mode="search" label="Matters" isSelected />
  <Chip mode="select" label="Trusts" onRemove={detachTrusts} />
  <Chip mode="filter" label="Status" value={{ label: 'Any', sections: statusSections }} onRemove={clearStatus} />
</ChipGroup>

antiExamples.name: Expecting overflow truncation
antiExamples.reason: Chip Group has no truncation - Figma models none, so all chips wrap onto new lines instead of collapsing behind a "+N more" affordance. `maxVisible` does not exist; use Tag Group (with Tags) when you need that behaviour. TypeScript rejects the prop.

antiExamples.name: Expecting the group to manage selection
antiExamples.reason: Chip Group is layout only. Search chips are independent on/off toggles, so which are selected is the consumer's state - pass isSelected/onSelectedChange to each Chip, exactly as with Toggle Button.

antiExamples.name: Repeating size on every chip inside a sized group
antiExamples.jsx:
<ChipGroup size="sm">
  <Chip mode="search" label="Matters" size="sm" />
  <Chip mode="search" label="Documents" size="sm" />
</ChipGroup>
antiExamples.reason: Redundant - the group already shares its size through context. Setting it per-chip is only for deliberately opting one chip out, and repeating it invites the exact bug the group exists to prevent: one chip missed, breaking the line it wraps onto.

antiExamples.name: Adding padding or a background to the group
antiExamples.reason: Chip Group is pure layout - Figma's own container has zero padding and no fill or stroke. Put the surface on a wrapper you own, so the group keeps hugging its chips.
